subject: Re: Post-call: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS for Acme Health integration
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS (next steps)

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time earlier — really helpful to see Acme Health's architecture and where Redwood would fit. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference to power clinical triage flows while keeping traffic off the public internet and meeting Acme's SOC2/networking requirements.
- Key technical asks you flagged: private connectivity (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink), IP allowlists for egress, control over DNS resolution (internal zones / split-horizon), and mutual TLS for client-to-server auth + cert rotation. Also asked about embeddings/reranker traffic patterns and SDK auth.

Proposed next steps
1) Share our VPC endpoint options and sample IP ranges (Marissa will attach a short options doc).
2) Map authentication options (API keys, mTLS, and token rotation) and recommended approach for your security team.
3) Run a short POC: staging VPC peering or PrivateLink + test prompt traffic (embeddings and reranking) to validate egress and latency.
4) Schedule an architecture session with your infra contact and our infra engineer (Marissa) — propose Mon/Tue next week.

Attachments: prox_arch_diagram.pdf (high-level flow); redwood_vpc_endpoint_options.pdf (short feature/ops doc)

Questions for you before the arch call
- Do you have a preference for PrivateLink vs VPC peering?
- Do you require inbound-only private endpoints (i.e., no outbound egress to public internet) or is controlled egress to Redwood-managed IPs acceptable?
- Who on your infra team should Marissa coordinate with for VPC setup?

I'll wait for your availability and any internal contacts. Dylan and I will prep a short checklist for your security team around SOC2 evidence for network controls.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS (next steps)

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the architecture call: 

1) IP allowlist / private endpoints
- We generally prefer PrivateLink-style endpoints (AWS) so traffic never traverses the public internet. Would Redwood provide an AWS PrivateLink service endpoint (i.e., private IPs in our VPC) or do you require a public egress with an allowlist?

2) DNS and split-horizon
- Our DNS team will want to point an internal A record (e.g., redwood-api.internal.acme) to the PrivateLink/endpoint. Confirm you support overriding the TLS SAN/hostname to match the internal name or if SNI passthrough is required.

3) mTLS and cert rotation
- We require mutual TLS for high-sensitivity flows. Does Redwood support client certificate authentication? If so, what's the cert rotation model and do you support automated rotation (ACME/Let’s Encrypt is not allowed in our environment — we use an internal CA)?

4) SDK/auth
- For embeddings and rerank traffic, is the SDK capable of token-based auth (short-lived tokens) vs long-lived API keys? Our security policy prefers short-lived tokens bound to service account creds.

5) Timeline and procurement
- We are targeting a pilot in Q2. Procurement will need a clear network requirements doc and SOC2 artifact. Can you share the specific IP ranges and ASN you use for egress (if any)?

If this is easier to cover live, happy to have our infra lead join the call — I can add them if you propose a couple of times.

Thanks,
Rajesh Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health
rajesh.patel@acmehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS (next steps)

Hi Rajesh —

Appreciate the questions — answers below at a high level. We'll cover the details in the architecture session but wanted to give immediate clarity so your procurement/DNS teams can plan.

1) Private connectivity options
- Redwood Hosted: we offer AWS PrivateLink endpoints for customers (PrivateLink is supported in most regions). This provides private IPs in your VPC and keeps traffic off the public internet.
- Redwood Dedicated/Private: For customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private, we can do VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or an on-prem gateway depending on your requirements. We’ll outline pros/cons in the attached PDF.

2) DNS & TLS/SNI
- DNS: we support split-horizon DNS; you can create an internal A/CNAME that resolves to the PrivateLink interface endpoint. For TLS, we support SNI-based routing; if you need the certificate to include an internal name, our infra team can support custom SANs for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted PrivateLink, SNI passthrough is the typical pattern — we’ll confirm exact SAN options in the call.

3) mTLS and cert rotation
- mTLS: supported. We support client certs presented by your services. For certificate management, we can accept certs issued by your internal CA. Rotation can be automated via an orchestration step you run (we can provide a small automation script and a checklist). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can integrate with your internal CA for automated rotation; for hosted PrivateLink we support periodic cert upload and provide an API for rotation. See mTLS checklist attached.

4) SDK & auth
- SDKs support both long-lived API keys and short-lived tokens. We recommend short-lived tokens for production (we provide a token-issuing service for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers can use scoped API keys with IP and usage restrictions).

5) IP ranges / egress
- For PrivateLink, egress to Redwood is over private interfaces; no public egress required. For hosted traffic that does egress, we maintain a published set of egress IP ranges (we'll send a CIDR list); we can also provide ASN info for firewall rules.

Next steps
- Marissa will propose specific CIDR blocks and a firewall checklist in a follow-up email.
- Can you share a preferred time for a 45-minute architecture session (include your infra lead) — Marissa is available Wed/Thu PST.

Attaching: redwood_vpc_endpoint_options.pdf, mTLS_rotation_checklist.docx

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Network specifics & staging playbook (Acme Health pilot)

Rajesh / team —

Thanks — looping in more technical details and a recommended staging checklist so your netops team can get started. Below are concise, actionable items and sample values you can drop into your firewall/DNS changes.

Network options (recommended)
- Option A (recommended): AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) — no public egress, private IPs in your VPC. Create Interface Endpoint(s) for the Redwood PrivateLink service in the subnets you want to reach the service from.
- Option B: VPC peering/Transit Gateway — good for Dedicated customers where you want a persistent routing relationship.

Sample CIDRs & ports (example only — will provide exact list after we validate account/region)
- Redwood PrivateLink interface endpoints: assigned in your VPC (no outbound egress required)
- If you need egress exceptions to our hosted egress: 34.208.128.0/18, 54.183.0.0/16 (sample only)
- Ports: 443 TCP (TLS) primarily; 80 only for health checks if required (HTTPS preferred).

DNS guidance
- Create an internal zone: redwood-api.internal.acme (or a CNAME) pointing to the interface endpoint ENI IPs.
- For SNI: configure your SNI to use external hostname the service expects (we can support SNI passthrough). If you require certs with internal SANs, we’ll scope that for Dedicated/Private.

mTLS checklist (high level)
- Auth mode: mTLS with client certs issued by Acme internal CA. We will validate client certs at connection time.
- Rotation: recommend 90-day rotation cadence; we can accept a short-lived envelope token model if you need faster rotation.
- Provisioning: provide a test cert for the staging environment, then work with our infra team to exchange thumbprints/CA chain.

Staging playbook (45–60 mins)
1) Provision PrivateLink interface endpoint(s) in staging VPC.
2) Create internal DNS A/CNAME to point to endpoint ENIs.
3) Upload/test client cert to Redwood staging endpoint or configure token-based exchange.
4) Run test harness: 1k small prompts + embeddings/rerank (to validate latency and egress behavior).
5) Review logs and traces in Redwood Console; we’ll share a short dashboard for the pilot.

What we need from you
- Preferred date/time for the arch session (Wed/Thu PST works for our team).
- Contact for your infra/DNS team (name + email).
- If you want us to provide exact egress CIDRs for firewall rules, confirm which region/hosted vs dedicated option you want to pilot.

I’ll attach a short firewall checklist and a step-by-step staging checklist after you confirm the pilot region. Happy to hop on a call with your infra lead and walk through the DNS and cert steps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Infrastructure Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
